segment_text: 20.1 Governing Further Actions. Each Party will execute, acknowledge and deliver such further instruments, and do all such other acts, as may be necessary or appropriate in order to carry out the purposes and intent of the Agreement.
span_text: Each Party will execute, acknowledge and deliver such further instruments, and do all such other acts, as may be necessary or appropriate in order to carry out the purposes and intent of the Agreement.
annotator_notes:
S2 of C04-174, a FURTHER-ASSURANCES clause. Batch 5, seed 20260919 hard queue, position 9 (positions 1-5 batch 4; 6 = E02-006, two items; 7 = E03-037 and 8 = E03-046, both excluded whole).

NO PRECEDENT EXISTED ON THE SUBSTANCE, which is why the class was measured rather than assumed. The further-assurances family recurs in this corpus (C17-064, C22-041, E05-020 and this segment), and the 'execute, acknowledge' triplet specifically appears in 2 of the 1,547 pool segments (C02-077 and this one) -- measured with a detector gated first on a known positive (this segment) AND a known negative (C04-180, the LOCKED counterparts-boilerplate exclusion, which is also 'execution boilerplate' and which a detector unable to separate the two would have swept in). THE ONE PRIOR ENCOUNTER IS ORTHOGONAL AND IS NAMED SO IT IS NOT MISREAD AS PRECEDENT: E05-020 is a further-assurances clause, but it was excluded as a MID-SENTENCE FRAGMENT (section 2 self-containment), so it rules on nothing here.

ONE ITEM, NOT TWO -- AND THE GROUND IS THE CATCH-ALL'S CONTENT, NOT THE SPAN COLLISION. REVIEWER-RULED 2026-09-24, and the order of the reasoning is itself part of the ruling so that a future catch-all is judged by content rather than by whether its span happens to collide.

  PRIMARY GROUND. 'and do all such other acts, as may be necessary or appropriate in order to carry out the purposes and intent of the Agreement' is a SWEEP-UP CLAUSE WITH NO DETERMINATE CONTENT OF ITS OWN. It is defined ENTIRELY BY REFERENCE to what 'execute, acknowledge and deliver such further instruments' does not happen to name -- 'such OTHER acts' means, by construction, the residue of the listed ones. Under section 4.3's corrected test (performance identity, not object identity) that is NOT a second performance: it is THE SAME PERFORMANCE'S SCOPE STATED BROADLY. Section 8.3's table row 2 ('genuinely separate objects -> two items') reads on its face as if instruments-versus-acts were two objects, and that surface reading is what this ruling declines: the test moved to section 4.3 at v0.28 precisely because object identity gives wrong answers, and this is an instance of it doing so.

  CORROBORATING EVIDENCE, EXPLICITLY NOT THE REASON. Splitting would force both items to carry the shared subject AND the shared trailing 'as may be necessary...' qualifier, so under section 8.3.1's v0.31 option 4 their spans would be near-identical and collide under section 4.1's IoU alignment -- the wall section 8.4 names in its own words ('both would carry a byte-identical span and collide under section 4.1's IoU alignment, the same wall section 8.3 hit'). This is a SYMPTOM of the underlying fact that there is only one performance here, and it corroborates the primary ground. It is not itself the ground, and a future catch-all whose span happened NOT to collide would still be one item on the primary ground alone.

BRANCH 3, NOT BRANCH 2 -- AND SECTION 8.3.2 FORECLOSES THE TEMPTING READING RATHER THAN THIS ITEM DECIDING IT FRESH. 'deliver' is a taxonomy member different from EXECUTE, so branch 1 fires regardless and compound_action is owed on any reading. The live question is 'acknowledge'. 'execute, acknowledge and deliver' is the classic deed-formality triplet, which invites branch 2's 'indemnify and hold harmless' exemption -- and section 8.3.2 refuses exactly that move in terms: branch 2 states its intuition 'as a mechanical mapping test, and extending it to a "feels like a legal doublet" judgment would trade a checkable boundary for an unfalsifiable one... what is refused is a branch-2 exemption with no mapping behind it.' There is NO named mapping for 'acknowledge', and under section 8.8.2's same-performance test acknowledging an instrument (formally attesting it) is not executing it (signing it). VERIFIED BY READING ast.py's real ACTIONS rather than from memory: EXECUTE in, DELIVER in, ACKNOWLEDGE out, DO out, PERFORM out. Both tags fire, which is E01-01's shape precisely.

  DROPPED VERBS, RECORDED VERBATIM as section 8.3 requires: 'acknowledge', 'deliver', and the catch-all 'do all such other acts'.

ACTION_ACCEPT_SET IS A SINGLETON, and the convention was read off the committed precedents rather than inferred. Branch 1 ALONE widens (C03-02: PROVIDE/DELIVER/MAINTAIN, its dropped verb being a taxonomy member); branch 3 does NOT (E01-01: ['WAIVE']; C10-01: ['INDEMNIFY']). This item is branch 3, so ['EXECUTE']. Section 8.8.5's G9 forced-choice disclosure therefore applies to it wherever criterion-2 figures are reported.

MUTUAL_OBLIGATION DOES NOT FIRE, worked through section 8.4.2's procedure IN ORDER rather than concluded from the 'Each Party' surface form -- which is the specific error that section's marker-regex paragraph warns about. (a) modality is duty-bearing: MUST, PASSES. (b) binds two or more parties: 'Each Party' is a distributive form the test names explicitly, PASSES. (c) the obligee is that same counterparty: NO obligee is stated anywhere in the span, and (c)'s own text rules that 'obligee: ABSENT is a FAILURE, not a deferral'. FAILS. No tag. Same outcome and same failing test as C04-02.

ELIGIBILITY CLEARS SECTION 2.5 / 2.5.1, checked rather than assumed because a further-assurances clause superficially resembles boilerplate. This is a DUTY, not a rights-reservation, so section 2.5's row does not reach it; and section 2.5.1's extension is to clauses vesting UNREVIEWABLE DISCRETION, which this has none of -- 'necessary or appropriate in order to carry out the purposes and intent of the Agreement' is a REVIEWABLE standard, unlike C11-046's 'sole business judgment' or C14-044's 'without any implication'. OPEN-ENDED SCOPE IS NOT UNREVIEWABLE DISCRETION: that is section 2.5.1's own negative worked example (C14-044) read in the other direction -- it warns that restricted scope does not supply monitorable stakes, and the converse holds too, unrestricted scope does not remove them where a reviewable standard governs.

MODALITY MUST. 'will' states a party's undertaking, not a future fact about the agreement -- section 3.2's will-ambiguity rule, the undertaking side.

CONDITIONS EMPTY. 'as may be necessary or appropriate in order to carry out the purposes and intent of the Agreement' fails section 3.8.2's removal test: delete it and the duty applies in exactly the same circumstances; what changes is WHICH instruments and acts it covers. That is object scope, the identical shape as E02-01's 'necessary for CBay to generate an invoice...' and consistent with E01-01's own conditions: [].

OBJECT_CLASS. Head noun of the object phrase ('such further instruments') is 'instrument', carried as the head-only member section 3.6's v0.58 forward rule requires of every item from batch 4 onward -- and it is the head noun OF THE OBJECT PHRASE, the bound C04-03's counter-example exists to enforce. SECTION 3.6.1 AND 3.6.2 BOTH CLEAR: no member restates the action (EXECUTE) or either party, and 'instrument' is not the nominal of EXECUTE, so clauses 2 and 5 stay independent here in a way they cannot for C22-01's NOTIFY/notice. 'execution_document' was DELIBERATELY NOT AUTHORED -- it would restate EXECUTE.

OBLIGEE = ABSENT. No counterparty is named anywhere in the span; the duty runs to whoever the Agreement's purposes require, which the sentence never states. Section 3.5's ordinary positional test, not a modality-driven default (section 3.5.4).

UNDERSPECIFIED TRUE ON TWO TRIGGERS, the first PROVABLE against a committed fixture rather than asserted: trigger 1 -- 'Each Party' does not resolve in evals/registry/C04.json, which holds only Miltenyi Biotec GmbH and Bellicum Pharmaceuticals, Inc. (verified by reading it); and the obligee is ABSENT. missing_fields carries both roles, the identical shape as E01-01.

COST TO THE PUBLISHED FIGURES, stated rather than left to be discovered. Both tags are REPRESENTATIONAL (verified in evals/harness/gap_kinds.py's GAP_KIND, not assumed), so section 9.1's kind-scoped in-force denominator EXCLUDES this item by construction and it can move the in-force criterion 2 in neither direction. It lands in the all-items figure only. C04-174 has no cassette, so the item is cassette-unscoreable today in any case and report.py's G8 will disclose it.

SPAN INCLUDES THE TRAILING PERIOD, per the measured gold convention (section 7.1's fourth finding: 19 of 31 matched items differ from the cold annotator only by a trailing '.', gold inclusive, zero the other way).

PROVENANCE. Segment text reproduces byte-for-byte against both the live corpus pool rebuild (1,547 segments, the pool's own known-answer gate) and batch04/draw.json. Sentence split produced by corpus.split_sentences(), gated first against locked segment E02-006's committed section 2.7 offsets (Standing Principle 7).

REVIEWER-APPROVED 2026-09-24. The one call put explicitly rather than approved by silence was the SPLIT: one item, ruled on the catch-all's lack of determinate content, with the span-collision argument demoted to corroborating evidence at the reviewer's direction so that a future catch-all is judged by content rather than by span geometry. Branch 3 tagging, the mutual_obligation failure and the object_class sizing were approved as drafted.
